_about: Plain-English wording for the Vyta report. score.py reads this file - edit the sentences here, no code changes needed.
_how_to_edit: Each indicator has three sentences: 'green' (what's going well and what to keep doing), 'amber' (a warning) and 'red' (a serious warning).
Words in {curly brackets} are filled in with real numbers when the report is made. Keep the curly brackets exactly as they are.
{value} and {threshold} are shown in the indicator's own units (e.g. '29 days', '91.8%', '0.58').
{threshold} is the Amber threshold in the Green and Amber sentences, and the Red threshold in the Red sentence.
{value_pct} / {threshold_pct} show a ratio as a percentage (0.58 -> 58%).
Each indicator can also use the extra figures listed in its '_also_available' line.
Sentences like 'red_overdrawn' or 'green_no_debt' are used instead of the normal one in a special case (e.g. the bank account is overdrawn, so there's no runway to calculate).
If a sentence uses a word in {brackets} that doesn't exist, score.py prints a note and leaves it as-is in the report.
Save the file, then re-run score.py. If score.py says the file is broken, check for a missing comma or quote.

D1.green: Short-term assets of {current_assets} comfortably cover short-term debts of {current_liabilities} ({value} times, above the {threshold} warning level). Keep this buffer in place, especially ahead of big bills like BAS or insurance.
D1.green_no_liabilities: The business has no short-term debts at the moment.
D1.amber: Short-term assets of {current_assets} are only {value} times short-term debts of {current_liabilities} (warning at {threshold}), leaving little buffer if bills fall due together.
D1.red: Short-term debts of {current_liabilities} are at least as large as short-term assets of {current_assets} (ratio {value}, Red at {threshold} or below), so the business may struggle to pay debts as they fall due.

D2.green: Cash plus money owed by customers ({cash_and_debtors}) covers {value_pct} of short-term debts of {current_liabilities}, above the {threshold_pct} warning level. Keep collecting from customers promptly to hold this position.
D2.green_no_liabilities: The business has no short-term debts at the moment.
D2.amber: Cash plus money owed by customers ({cash_and_debtors}) covers only {value_pct} of short-term debts of {current_liabilities} (warning at {threshold_pct}).
D2.red: Cash plus money owed by customers ({cash_and_debtors}) covers only {value_pct} of short-term debts of {current_liabilities} (Red at {threshold_pct} or below), so paying what is already owed depends on future sales or new funding.

D3.green: At the recent rate of spending, cash of {cash} would last about {value}, above the {threshold} warning level. Aim to keep at least {threshold} of costs in reserve.
D3.green_not_falling: Cash isn't falling: it went from {cash_before} at {month_before} to {cash} at {month}. Keep building a reserve to carry the business through quieter months.
D3.amber: At the recent rate of spending ({monthly_outflow} a month), cash of {cash} would last about {value} (warning at {threshold} or less).
D3.red: At the recent rate of spending ({monthly_outflow} a month), cash of {cash} would run out in about {value} (Red at {threshold} or less).
D3.red_overdrawn: There is no cash buffer: the bank balance is {cash} (overdrawn) at {month}, so any unexpected bill has to be met from the overdraft or new funding.

D4.green: The ATO balance ({ato_now}) isn't building up month after month, a good sign that tax is being paid on time. Keep lodging and paying BAS, PAYG and super by their due dates.
D4.amber: The ATO balance has risen for {value} months in a row, to {ato_now}. This can be normal in the run-up to a BAS payment, but check it is paid in full when due.
D4.red: The ATO balance has risen for {value} months in a row (Red at {threshold} months or more), from {ato_start} to {ato_now}. Growing tax debt is one of the clearest early signs of a cash problem, and unpaid PAYG, GST and super can lead to director penalty notices.

D5.green: Bank loans and overdraft changed by {value} over six months ({debt_before} to {debt_now}), below the {threshold} warning level, so the business isn't leaning on extra borrowing. Keep paying debt down where you can.
D5.green_no_debt: The business has no bank loans or overdraft, so it isn't relying on borrowing to fund day-to-day costs.
D5.amber: Bank loans and overdraft have grown {value} in six months, from {debt_before} to {debt_now} (warning at {threshold}).
D5.red: Bank loans and overdraft have grown {value} in six months, from {debt_before} to {debt_now} (Red at {threshold}), which suggests borrowing is being used to cover cash shortfalls.
D5.red_new_debt: The business has taken on {debt_now} of bank debt or overdraft in the last six months, having had none at {month_before}.

D6.green: The overdraft is {value} drawn ({overdraft} of a {limit} limit), leaving headroom for unexpected costs. Keep it as a safety net rather than a permanent source of funding.
D6.amber: The overdraft is {value} drawn ({overdraft} of a {limit} limit; warning at {threshold}), leaving little room for unexpected costs.
D6.red: The overdraft is at or over its limit: {overdraft} drawn against a {limit} limit ({value}; Red at {threshold}). The bank may refuse further payments.

D7.green: Suppliers are paid in about {value} on average, inside the {threshold} warning level. Paying on time protects supplier relationships and credit terms, so keep it up.
D7.amber: Suppliers are being paid in about {value} on average (warning at {threshold}), which can start to strain supplier relationships.
D7.red: Suppliers are waiting about {value} on average to be paid (Red at {threshold}), with {creditors} owed. Suppliers may stop offering credit or start chasing the debt.

D8.green: Only {value} of unpaid supplier bills ({overdue_90} of {total_unpaid}) are more than 90 days overdue. Keep paying suppliers within their terms.
D8.green_nothing_unpaid: There are no unpaid supplier bills.
D8.green_none_overdue: None of the {total_unpaid} in unpaid supplier bills is more than 90 days overdue. Keep paying suppliers within their terms.
D8.amber: {value} of unpaid supplier bills ({overdue_90} of {total_unpaid}) are more than 90 days overdue (warning at {threshold}).
D8.red: {value} of unpaid supplier bills ({overdue_90} of {total_unpaid}) are more than 90 days overdue (Red at {threshold}). Long-overdue suppliers are the most likely source of a statutory demand.

D9.green: Customers are paying about as quickly as before, or faster: debtor days moved from {days_before} to {days_now} over three months. Keep invoicing promptly and following up late payers.
D9.amber: Customers are taking longer to pay: debtor days rose by {value} in three months, from {days_before} to {days_now} (warning at a rise of {threshold}).
D9.red: Customers are taking much longer to pay: debtor days rose by {value} in three months, from {days_before} to {days_now} (Red at a rise of {threshold}). More cash is being tied up in unpaid invoices.

D10.green: Only {value} of money owed by customers ({overdue_90} of {total_unpaid}) is more than 90 days overdue. Keep following up invoices as soon as they fall due.
D10.green_nothing_unpaid: No customers owe the business money at the moment.
D10.green_none_overdue: None of the {total_unpaid} owed by customers is more than 90 days overdue. Keep following up invoices as soon as they fall due.
D10.amber: {value} of money owed by customers ({overdue_90} of {total_unpaid}) is more than 90 days overdue (warning at {threshold}). Some of it may not be collectable.
D10.red: {value} of money owed by customers ({overdue_90} of {total_unpaid}) is more than 90 days overdue (Red at {threshold}). It may need to be written off, and it is worth finding out why these customers aren't paying.

D11.green: There's no sign of sales growth draining cash. As sales grow, keep an eye on stock levels and how quickly customers pay.
D11.amber: Sales have been rising while cash has fallen for {value} months in a row (warning at {threshold} months). Cash may be going into stock, slow-paying customers or costs.
D11.red: Sales have been rising while cash has fallen for {value} months in a row (Red at {threshold} months or more). Growth is using up cash faster than it comes in, so find out where the cash is going.

D12.green: Day-to-day trading generated an estimated {ocf} over the year, enough to cover {value_pct} of short-term debts of {current_liabilities}. The business is funding itself from trading, which is the strongest position to be in.
D12.green_no_liabilities: The business has no short-term debts at the moment.
D12.amber: Day-to-day trading generated an estimated {ocf} over the year, enough to cover only {value_pct} of short-term debts of {current_liabilities} (warning at {threshold_pct}).
D12.red: Day-to-day trading generated an estimated {ocf} over the year, enough to cover only {value_pct} of short-term debts of {current_liabilities} (Red at {threshold_pct} or below). Trading alone isn't producing the cash needed to pay what is owed.
D12.red_negative: Day-to-day trading used more cash than it brought in over the year (an estimated {ocf}), so none of the short-term debts of {current_liabilities} are being paid for by trading.

D13.green: Debts of {total_liabilities} are {value_pct} of total assets of {total_assets}, below the {threshold_pct} warning level, so the business isn't over-reliant on borrowing.
D13.amber: Debts of {total_liabilities} equal {value_pct} of total assets of {total_assets} (warning at {threshold_pct}), so most of the business is funded by borrowing.
D13.red: Debts of {total_liabilities} are at or above total assets of {total_assets} ({value_pct}; Red at {threshold_pct}). Even selling everything would not repay all debts.
D13.red_no_assets: The business has no assets recorded against debts of {total_liabilities}.

V1.green: Owners' equity is {value_pct} of total assets (net assets {net_assets}), a solid buffer to absorb a bad patch. Keeping profits in the business keeps it strong.
V1.amber: Owners' equity is only {value_pct} of total assets (net assets {net_assets}; warning at {threshold_pct}), so there is a thin buffer to absorb losses.
V1.red: The business owes more than it owns: net assets are {net_assets} (equity ratio {value_pct}; Red at {threshold_pct} or below). This is a serious warning sign, although Australian insolvency is judged on whether debts can be paid as they fall due.
V1.red_no_assets: The business has no assets recorded, so there is nothing to absorb losses (net assets {net_assets}).

V2.green: Gross margin is {value}, above the {threshold} warning level, leaving room to cover overheads and invest. Review prices regularly so rising costs don't erode it.
V2.amber: Gross margin is {value} (warning at {threshold}), leaving limited room to cover overheads and repay debt.
V2.red: Gross margin is only {value} (Red at {threshold}). Each sale leaves very little to pay overheads, so pricing or direct costs need attention.

V3.green: Gross margin has held steady or improved over the year ({margin_before} to {margin_now}). Keep watching supplier costs and discounting to protect it.
V3.amber: Gross margin slipped from {margin_before} to {margin_now} over the past year ({value}; warning at {threshold}).
V3.red: Gross margin fell sharply over the past year, from {margin_before} to {margin_now} ({value}; Red at {threshold}). Rising costs or discounting are eroding the profit on every sale.

V4.green: Overheads of {opex} use {value} of gross profit ({gross_profit}), below the {threshold} warning level, so the business is a sustainable size for its sales. Keep overheads growing more slowly than gross profit.
V4.amber: Overheads of {opex} use up {value} of gross profit ({gross_profit}; warning at {threshold}), leaving little profit.
V4.red: Overheads of {opex} use up {value} of gross profit ({gross_profit}; Red at {threshold}). The business is too big for its current sales unless overheads come down or margins go up.
V4.red_no_gross_profit: The business made no gross profit over the year ({gross_profit}), so nothing is left to pay overheads of {opex}.

V5.green: Underlying profit is {underlying_profit}, {value} of revenue, so the core business makes money. This is the most important sign that the business is viable.
V5.amber: Underlying profit (before interest, depreciation and one-off costs) is {underlying_profit}, only {value} of revenue (warning at {threshold}).
V5.red: Even before interest, depreciation and one-off costs, the business is not making money: underlying profit is {underlying_profit} ({value} of revenue; Red at {threshold}). Fixing the cash problem alone would not make it viable.

V6.green: Revenue has held up or grown over the year ({revenue_before} to {revenue_now}, {value}). Keep investing in what is bringing customers in.
V6.amber: Revenue fell from {revenue_before} to {revenue_now} over the past year ({value}; warning at {threshold}).
V6.red: Revenue dropped sharply over the past year, from {revenue_before} to {revenue_now} ({value}; Red at {threshold}). Demand for what the business sells is shrinking.

V7._also_available: (none yet - Xero Quotes are not pulled)
V7.green: Open quotes cover {value} months of average revenue, so there is work lined up.
V7.amber: Open quotes cover only {value} months of average revenue (warning at {threshold}).
V7.red: Open quotes cover only {value} months of average revenue (Red at {threshold}), so there is little work lined up.

V8.green: Long-term assets of {nca} cover long-term debts of {ncl} ({value} times), giving lenders good security if the business ever needs to refinance.
V8.green_no_long_term_liabilities: The business has no long-term debt.
V8.amber: Long-term assets of {nca} only just cover long-term debts of {ncl} (ratio {value}; warning at {threshold}), which limits options to refinance.
V8.red: Long-term debts of {ncl} are larger than long-term assets of {nca} (ratio {value}; Red at {threshold}), so lenders have little security to support refinancing.

_verdicts_help: The one-sentence headline at the top of the dashboard and PDF: what the business's situation is. {org} = business name. Keep it to the situation; the action goes in 'pathways' below so the two don't repeat each other.

Low.Strong: {org} is in good financial health: it is trading profitably and paying its debts on time.
Low.Uncertain: {org} has no immediate cash pressure, but its profitability isn't yet convincing.
Low.Weak: {org} is paying its way for now, but the business itself isn't making money.

Moderate.Strong: {org} is a sound business that is starting to feel cash pressure.
Moderate.Uncertain: {org} is under growing cash pressure, and it isn't clear the business is profitable enough to fix it.
Moderate.Weak: {org} is under cash pressure, and the business isn't making money.

High.Strong: {org} is under serious cash and debt pressure, but the underlying business makes money.
High.Uncertain: {org} is in serious financial distress, and it isn't clear the business can recover.
High.Weak: {org} is in serious financial distress, and the business isn't making money.

verdict_not_enough_data: There isn't enough data yet to reach a verdict on {org}.
_pathways_help: Shown under 'Recommended pathway', straight after the pathway name from scorecard.json (e.g. 'Urgent advice: assess restructure vs liquidation'). Add the why or the first step - don't restate the pathway name or the verdict.

Low.Strong: Keep doing what is working and protect the cash buffer.
Low.Uncertain: Do it now, while there is no cash pressure forcing rushed decisions.
Low.Weak: Start with the indicators above: they show where the business is losing money.

Moderate.Strong: Acting now, while the business is still profitable, keeps the most options open.
Moderate.Uncertain: An adviser can help trace where the cash has gone and build a turnaround plan.
Moderate.Weak: Get professional advice soon: the longer cash pressure runs, the fewer options remain.

High.Strong: Get insolvency advice now: a formal restructure works best when it starts early.
High.Uncertain: Speak to a registered insolvency practitioner now; acting early keeps more options open.
High.Weak: A registered insolvency practitioner can advise on the safest way to close or sell, and on directors' obligations.

pathway_not_enough_data: There isn't enough data yet to place the business on the outcome matrix.
_data_confidence_help: Shown with the scores. {months} = months with trading activity, {of} = months looked at (usually 12).

data_confidence.High: Based on a full {months} of {of} months of trading data.
data_confidence.Medium: Based on {months} of {of} months of trading data. Trends and yearly figures may shift as more months come in.
data_confidence.Low: Only {months} of {of} months have trading activity, so these scores rest on limited data. Treat them as an early indication and re-check once more months are available.

_cash_page_help: Dashboard Cash page. {start}/{end} = month names, {months} = months covered. Step names must match cashflow.py.

cash_page.title: Where has the cash gone?
cash_page.intro: How cash moved from {start} to {end} ({months} months). Each bar adds to or takes away from the opening balance.
cash_page.short_history: Only 12 months of data were available, so this starts at the first month-end ({start}).

steps.Operating profit: Net profit from the profit and loss report for these months.
steps.ATO movement: A rising ATO balance keeps cash in the business for now, but it is a debt that must be paid.
steps.Debt movement: New bank loans bring cash in; repayments take it out. Overdrafts are already inside cash.
steps.Change in debtors: When customers owe more, sales have been made but the cash has not been collected yet.
steps.Change in creditors: When the business owes suppliers more, it has held on to cash by paying later.
steps.Other: Everything else, such as owner drawings, buying or selling equipment, and non-cash costs like depreciation.

indicators_page.intro: Each line shows the last 12 month-ends, worked out with the same formula as the score. Click Details for the full trend.
indicators_page.short_history: Earlier points use whatever months were available up to that month-end, so the first few may cover less than a full year.

_whatif_page_help: Dashboard What if? page. {levers} = the lever phrases joined with commas and 'and'; {d_before}/{d_after} = distress bands, {v_before}/{v_after} = viability bands. The sentence is given a capital letter automatically.

whatif_page.heading: See how a change would move the scores
whatif_page.intro: Try changes to the business and see how the scores would move. Nothing here changes the real scores or the data.

levers.ato_plan: putting the ATO debt on a 12-month payment plan

whatif_page.moves_both: {levers} moves this business from {d_before} to {d_after} distress and from {v_before} to {v_after} viability.
whatif_page.moves_distress: {levers} moves this business from {d_before} to {d_after} distress.
whatif_page.moves_viability: {levers} moves this business from {v_before} to {v_after} viability.
whatif_page.no_change: {levers} doesn't change either band: distress stays {d_before} and viability stays {v_before}.
whatif_page.pathway_change: The recommended pathway changes from {before} to {after}.
whatif_page.no_levers: Move a slider to see how the scores would change.
whatif_page.assumptions: How this works: price, volume, cost and overhead changes are applied to each of the last 12 months, and the extra profit is assumed to arrive as cash. Faster collection turns that many days of sales from debtors into cash at the latest month-end. The ATO payment plan pays the first of 12 equal instalments from cash at the latest month-end. Unpaid-invoice ageing (D8, D10), depreciation and interest are left as they are.

_owner_questions_page_help: Dashboard Owner questions page. Answers are entered in scorecard.json (the "answer" field of each question).

owner_questions_page.heading: What only the owner can tell us
owner_questions_page.intro: Some things can't be read from Xero. These answers sharpen the scores; until they're in, the related checks stay out of the scores.
owner_questions_page.how_to_answer: To record an answer, add it to the "answer" field of the question in scorecard.json, then refresh this page.
owner_questions_page.waiting_none: No indicators are waiting on owner input.

_history_page_help: Dashboard History page (snapshots saved by sync.py). Placeholders: {date} in 'one'; {before} and {after} (the two snapshot dates) in 'changes_sub' and 'changes_none'.

history_page.title: History
history_page.heading: How the scores have moved
history_page.intro: Each time the data is refreshed, Vyta saves both scores and every indicator's result. This page shows how they have moved.
history_page.none: No history yet. A snapshot is saved each time the data is refreshed: press Refresh now, or wait for the daily 7am update.
history_page.one: One snapshot so far, from {date}. The charts and the list of changes start once there are two.
history_page.changes_sub: Indicators that changed colour between {before} and {after}.
history_page.changes_none: No indicator changed colour between {before} and {after}.

_refresh_help: The Last updated line and Refresh now button in the dashboard's top bar.

refresh.help_xero: Pulls the latest figures from Xero (read-only), rebuilds and re-scores. Takes about a minute.
refresh.help_offline: Rebuilds and re-scores this test business from its saved files. Xero isn't contacted.
refresh.running: Refreshing - this takes about a minute...

_pathway_labels_help: Short name for each pathway (distress band, then viability band), shown on the Overview banner and the Get help page.
_shell_help: The parts shown on every page: sidebar, top bar. {end} is the last month-end.

shell.connected_text: Read-only. Vyta never changes your books.
shell.sample_text: A made-up test business. Not connected to Xero.
shell.demo_text: Two made-up businesses. Not connected to Xero, and nothing you do here is saved.
shell.get_listed: Are you an adviser? Get listed

_overview_page_help: Dashboard Overview page. {count} in issues_link is the number of indicators.

overview_page.viability_question: Is there a business worth saving?
overview_page.issues_none: No indicators are flagged Red or Amber.
overview_page.footer: Indicative early-warning signals based on Xero data, not an insolvency determination or professional advice.

_details_page_help: Dashboard Details page. 'figures' maps a column of monthly_summary.csv to its label (shown in this order). {date} is the last month-end.

details_page.title: The numbers behind the scores
details_page.intro: Every indicator, what it measured and where it sits against its warning levels. Select a row to see what it means.

questions.distress: How much financial trouble is the business in right now?
questions.viability: If the cash problem were fixed, would the business make money?

_help_page_help: Dashboard Get help page. The firms themselves are in firms.json. {date} etc. are not used here.

help_page.title: Advisers matched to where your business is
help_page.intro: Matched on your pathway and what your results show, with advisers in your state listed first. You choose who to contact. Vyta never shares your data or scores.
help_page.none: No listed advisers of this type match your pathway yet.
help_page.how_text: Listed partners pay a flat fee to appear here. Vyta takes no commission on appointments. Registered liquidators are checked against ASIC's register before listing.
help_page.adviser_text: Reach businesses that need your help, early. Listings are reviewed against our criteria before going live.
help_page.apply_text: Adviser listings aren't open yet. This page shows how they will look.
help_page.sample_note: This is a fictional sample listing. The details are placeholders and don't belong to a real firm.
help_page.privacy_note: Vyta doesn't send your data or scores to anyone. You decide what to share when you get in touch.
help_page.footer: Sample listings shown are fictional, for design purposes only. Listings are general information, not a recommendation or professional advice.
